title: Extract experimental activity data
action: Digitise or manually extract the activity–composition data points for YH2-δ (Yannopoulos et al., 1965), CeH2+δ (Lundin, 1966), and ThC1-δ (Satow, 1967) at all reported temperatures. Format each dataset as a CSV file with columns: temperature, composition_delta, activity_X. For ThC1-δ, convert the composition to δ in CTh1+δ notation (M = C, X = Th). Compress the three CSV files into a single zip archive.

title: Compute diagnostic variables and perform linear regression
action: For each system and each temperature isotherm, compute y and x for every candidate defect model using the formulas given in the Approach section (negative deviation set for YH2-δ, positive deviation set for CeH2+δ and CTh1+δ). Perform ordinary least-squares linear regression of y on x for each model; record R², slope, and intercept. Write the diagnostic data to diagnostics.csv.
description: Diagnostic data for all systems, including x_i, y_i, R_squared, slope, and intercept for each defect model at each temperature. Enables the verifier to recompute the linear regressions and extract interaction energies.
output_schema: columns: system, defect_model, temperature, x_i, y_i, R_squared, slope, intercept

title: Extract interaction energies and formation parameters
action: From the slopes of the best-fit models in diagnostics.csv, compute the interaction free energies ξ using the conversion formulas and structural parameters presented in the Approach. For YH2-δ, fit ξ vs. T to obtain the vacancy-pair formation enthalpy and entropy. Write the final results to results.json.
description: Final results: identified defect type for each system, interaction energies ξ at each temperature, and for YH2-δ the vacancy-pair formation enthalpy and entropy.
